title: Persistent Says Employee Immigration Data May Be Exfiltrated From US Law Firm
excerpt: The breach was at a US law firm handling Persistent's immigration matters, not the company's own systems, the Pune IT major told stock exchanges — without naming the firm or how many employees are affected.
body:
• Persistent Systems said on Monday that a US-based law firm it engaged for immigration matters may have experienced a cybersecurity incident, and certain employee immigration data and supporting documentation was purportedly exfiltrated from that law firm.
  • The incident was at the external law firm, not Persistent's own systems: the company said its systems are secure and business operations continue as usual.
  • Claims that critical company information was stolen are unverified, Persistent said, because the law firm was not in possession of such information.
  • What is not yet known — and not stated in the filing: the law firm's name, when the incident occurred, and how many employees are affected. Affected employees should watch for a direct notification from the company rather than acting on unverified claims.

Persistent Systems, the Pune-based IT services company, has disclosed that employee immigration data may have been taken from a US law firm that handles its immigration matters. In a stock exchange filing on Monday, the company said the law firm may have experienced a cybersecurity incident in which certain employee immigration data and supporting documents could have been extracted.

""Claims that the Company's critical information was stolen are unverified as the law firm was not in possession of such information," the filing said."

"We are aware that a U.S.-based law firm that Persistent Systems engaged for immigration matters of the company may have experienced a cybersecurity incident, and certain of our employee immigration data and supporting documentation was purportedly exfiltrated from that law firm," the company said, in a filing reported by IANS.

What Persistent says — and what it does not say

The company was explicit about where the incident sits. It was related to the external law firm and not to Persistent's own systems, which are secure, with business operations continuing as usual. "Claims that the Company's critical information was stolen are unverified as the law firm was not in possession of such information," the filing said.

The filing does not identify the law firm, disclose when the incident occurred, or specify how many employees may be affected. It also does not detail the categories of immigration documents that may have been exposed. Immigration files, by their nature, are document-heavy — they are assembled to support visa and work-authorization cases — which is why the distinction the company draws matters: the exposure it describes is of employee immigration data held by an outside firm, not of Persistent's client systems or its own network.

How the market read it

Persistent's shares gained during Monday's session amid overall buying momentum for IT stocks in a weak market. NSE data showed the shares rising 2.7% to an intraday high of ₹6,295, against a previous close of ₹6,124, according to Upstox, which also put the company's market capitalisation at ₹1.04 lakh crore in Monday's session.

What affected employees should watch for

For Persistent employees with US immigration cases handled through the firm — a group that includes staff on assignment in the United States — the filing is a disclosure, not a set of instructions. It names no steps employees must take, and no deadline. The next concrete development to watch is whether the company or the law firm notifies affected individuals directly with what data was involved. Until then, the company's position stands as stated: its own systems are secure, operations are normal, and claims beyond employee immigration data are unverified.
